extracted.intended_audience: IP attorneys, patent agents, law firm/practice managers, corporate counsel, and researchers interested in IP services pricing
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of the metrics and reporting standards used in the AIPLA 2023 Economic Survey for measuring charges, billing methods, demographics, and litigation costs for IP services. Focuses on how respondents were asked to report fees and the specific metrics presented (medians, means, fee types, service categories, and cost components).

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction for reporting typical charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey respondents were asked to report typical charges for 63 IP law services—but only if they had been personally responsible for a representative sample of the work involved either as a service provider or as a service purchaser.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charges were to be based on cases with no unusual complications and were to include legal services only (no copy, drawing, or government fees). The 63 services were grouped under six headings. Note on comparability: questions were added to the firm survey in 2019 only where the data from both surveys were combined to present the 2018 charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service grouping / categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The 63 surveyed services are grouped into six headings: Trademarks (including Service Marks) [12 services], US Utility Patents including foreign-origin patents where no substantive direction is received from foreign attorneys [26 services], US Utility Patents of Foreign Origin in which foreign attorneys provide substantive direction (exclude government, foreign associates, drawing and similar fees) [10 services], Filing US Applications Abroad (Europe - EPO) [7 services], Other US Patents and Copyrights [6 services], and Transactional Work [2 services].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grouping is used to present median charges for each service across years; comparisons across groups should account for category definitions and excluded fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Median charge per service (time series 2008–2022)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each of the listed services the survey reports median charges (and often 1st/3rd quartile, mean) for multiple years (2008, 2010, 2012, 2014, 2016, 2018, 2020, 2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medians are the principal central-tendency metric reported; many tables also include quartiles, means, and respondent counts. Use medians for typical charge comparisons; compare years cautiously because of survey population/composition changes (e.g., full-time only vs earlier mixed respondents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of fee for service charges (fixed vs hourly vs other)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each service the survey reports the primary type of fee used in 2022: percent fixed fee, percent hourly, percent other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report highlights which services are most likely billed hourly or on a fixed-fee basis (category-specific lists provided). Median fees are displayed separately for respondents who primarily use fixed fees vs hourly where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Services most likely billed hourly — Trademarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Within trademarks, the following services are most likely billed on an hourly basis: Trademark Appeal to the Board (Briefed/Argued) (81.2%), Trademark Prosecution (Total, incl. amendments/interviews but not appeals) (74.3%), Preparing a UDRP Petition (71.8%), Responding to a UDRP Petition (71.6%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversely, certain trademark services (registration application, renewal, Section 8 & 15, Statement of Use) are most likely billed on a fixed-fee basis (percentages listed). Use these percentages to classify typical billing method by trademark service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Services most likely billed hourly — US Utility Patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Within US utility patents, services most likely billed hourly include Infringement/Non-infringement Only Opinion (79.3%), Combination Validity and Infringement (79.0%), Validity/Invalidity Only Opinion (77.8%), Appeal to Board with oral argument (71.9%), Ex parte re-exam (71.3%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other patent services (paying maintenance fee, preparing/filling IDS <50 refs, issuing allowed application) are most likely billed on a fixed-fee basis. The report provides percent breakdowns and separate median fee figures by fixed vs hourly respondent designation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Services most likely billed hourly or fixed — US Utility Patents of Foreign Origin
rubrics_metrics.description: For US utility patents of foreign origin, the survey identifies services most likely billed hourly (e.g., certain amendment/argument work where foreign counsel/client provides detailed instructions) and services most likely billed on fixed fee (e.g., paying an annuity/maintenance fee 70.8%, entering national stage in US receiving office 68.4%, filing foreign-origin utility patent app in USPTO ready for filing 67.8%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Percentages for fixed vs hourly vs other are provided per service; use to infer billing norms for work involving foreign-origin matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Services most likely billed hourly or fixed — Filing US Applications Abroad (Europe - EPO)
rubrics_metrics.description: For filing US-origin applications abroad (EPO), the survey lists amendment/argument work (various tech areas) that are most likely billed hourly (e.g., mechanical amendments ~69.0%), while paying annuity/maintenance fee (60.5%) and entering national stage (46.2%) are relatively more likely fixed-fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides percent breakdowns by service; useful for pricing expectations when engaging foreign counsel or coordinating cross-border filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Services most likely billed hourly or fixed — Other US Patents and Copyrights
rubrics_metrics.description: Responding to office action in design patent applications (67.7%) and US plant patent app prep/file (57.5%) are most likely billed hourly. Copyright registration preparation and US design patent application prep/file are more likely billed fixed fee (percentages provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Percent breakdowns included; interpret median fees with awareness of the primary billing type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Services most likely billed hourly — Transactional Work
rubrics_metrics.description: Transactional services are overwhelmingly billed hourly: Due diligence (92.9%) and Preparing licenses, including negotiations (92.2%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transactional matters are almost always hourly per the 2022 survey; fixed-fee usage for these services is minimal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Median and quartile presentation for category charts (visual summaries)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each major category (Trademarks, US Utility Patents, US Utility Patents of Foreign Origin, Filing Abroad-EPO, Other US Patents & Copyrights, Transactional Work) the report displays 1st quartile, median, mean, 3rd quartile values in bar/box visuals for typical charges and costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use quartiles to understand distribution/skew; mean can be heavily influenced by high outliers, so median and quartiles are preferred for 'typical' charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surcharge to clients for handling invoices from foreign counsel (Europe – EPO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey asks whether firms surcharge clients for handling invoices from foreign counsel for Europe (EPO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported result: No 77.8%, Yes 22.2%. Use to assess common firm billing practices for foreign counsel pass-through costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private firm, patent agent compensation and demographics metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics reported for private firm patent agents include average age, highest degree distribution (e.g., percent holding doctorate, master's), average years of IP non-attorney experience, gender and racial composition, median and mean 2022 full-time total gross income, median expected 2023 gross income, average year-end cash bonus, median employer 401(k)/403(b) contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report notes comparability caveats (e.g., 2022 income figures limited to full-time respondents whereas earlier years may have included part-time respondents). Also includes percent time spent on IP prosecution and percent devoted to patents, median number of new priority US and PCT applications prepared/filed, median billable hours, median average hourly billing rate, and billing method proportions (hourly vs fixed vs discounted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Workload and productivity metrics for patent agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes median number of new priority US and PCT patent applications prepared/ filed in 2022 (median 20.0, average 21.8), median billable hours (1,500), median average hourly billing rate ($275), and percent of services billed hourly vs predetermined fee vs discounted hourly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to benchmark individual or firm-level productivity and billing rates; historical comparisons included for multiple years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical costs of litigation — reporting scope and components
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey collected respondent estimates of total litigation costs only for types of litigation they had personal knowledge of; 'Total cost' includes outside legal and paralegal services, local counsel, associates, paralegals, travel and living expenses, court reporter fees/costs, photocopies, courier services, exhibit preparation, analytical testing, expert witnesses, translators, surveys, jury advisors, and similar expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents were asked to estimate costs based on a single IP asset (one patent at issue, one trademark, etc.) and for matters engaged in relatively recently. Use reported totals as end-to-end cost estimates including expert and ancillary expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent-count and fixed-vs-hourly median fee split
rubrics_metrics.description: For many services the report tabulates separate medians for respondents who primarily use fixed fees versus those who primarily use hourly fees, and provides respondent counts for each cell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing median fixed vs hourly fees, consider respondent counts (some medians based on small N) and the report's caution about using caution where very few respondents reported a fee type (especially for some transactional items).
